members.reason: Proposes allocating needed resources (budgets, materials, tools) to research ventures — the resource-allocation lever.
Proposes allocating financial resources (funding for equipment, staff, expenses) — same allocate-resources-to-research intervention; a supporter of one could not oppose the other.
Citizen science: recruit the broad public into collecting and co-creating scientific knowledge.
Mediating science from academia to citizen-science volunteers with the explicit goal of involving masses in the research process — same public-participation-in-research lever.
States the purpose of the same convening ('the goal of the convening is...') — a culture of discussion producing agreements; a fragment of the identical proposal, not an independent value statement.
Convene stakeholders representing the range of opinions in a periodic forum for discussion and agreement — the concrete action both members describe.
Concrete proposal: researchers must collaborate with end users affected by the research subject.
'Combining knowledge and involvement for environmental change' is a vague sentiment naming no actor and no action — not interchangeable with the specific end-user-collaboration proposal.
Proposes building understanding of the place through information layers and identified needs.
'Information vacuum' is a bare problem statement, not a proposal — problem merged with solution violates the rubric.
Concrete proposal: give appropriate incentives and supports for carrying out the change.
'Connected to economic benefit' is a fragment/sentiment about economics, not the give-incentives-and-supports intervention itself.
Simplify research problems into accessible, non-threatening, clear discourse tailored to different sectors and bodies.
'Speak the language of the target audience' is the same audience-adapted-communication lever, just terser.
Core proposal: multi-axis collaborations (cross-discipline, cross-campus, cross-rank, cross-sector) aimed at concrete impact.

Cooperation with the local authority to align projects with community needs is one narrow slice — same topic (partnerships) but a much narrower, different-scope intervention; a supporter of municipal coordination need not endorse cross-campus/cross-rank academic collaboration.
Deepen knowledge across trans-disciplines and seek solutions in diverse directions — the cross-disciplinary-research lever.
Promote multidisciplinary research combining social sciences, exact sciences and technology to solve complex problems — same intervention.
Concrete proposal: map existing knowledge sources (prior research, data) as a base for research-field collaboration.
'Successful collaboration' is a two-word sentiment with no action — not the knowledge-mapping proposal.
Personal acquaintance with a person who researched and understands the topic — the direct-personal-connection lever.
Same lever stated with a venue: personal acquaintance is the key, via conferences emphasizing unmediated human connection.
A connecting agent who presents the data clearly and makes the interpersonal connection between researcher and actors — the intermediation lever.
'Matchmaking' researchers with civil-society orgs and ministries is the same create-the-connector intervention; a supporter of one could not reasonably oppose the other.
Concrete proposal: physical meetings between academics and practitioners for knowledge sharing and collaboration.

'Connecting people is critical, promote initiatives that bring people with different ideas together' is a general value statement without the specific physical academia-practitioner meeting lever — sentiment merged with a concrete proposal.
Provide funding/resources (plus freedom of action) to enable implementation and cross-sector collaborations — resource-provision lever.
Provide resources (information access, tools, budgets, workshops) supporting academia-practitioner collaborations — same intervention.
Interpersonal relationships as the bridge between research and the field, enabling clear data transfer — the personal-relationship lever.
Build long-term personal connections between research representatives and the field via meetings and workshops — same intervention with implementation detail.
Meaningful motivation, patience and persistence from those driving the change — the perseverance disposition.
Stubbornness/consistency and commitment throughout the research despite challenges — the same perseverance disposition, interchangeable.
Core claim: successful environmental struggles balanced scientific validity with activist passion — combine science with passion.

Combining emotion toward the environment with a sense of self-efficacy pairs different ingredients (emotion + efficacy, no scientific-validity component) — same emotional-mobilization topic but a different combination, not interchangeable.
'Research can drive big things' is a pure value/sentiment statement with no action — not the strengthen-applied-research proposal.
Core proposal: strengthen applied research so research contributes to changing reality.
Developing scientific tools to promote solutions/policy change is a different lever (build tools) from strengthening applied research — same topic, different intervention.
Make research's power practical and implementable so knowledge does not stay theoretical — same applied/practical-research intervention as the core.
Establish partnerships with academic institutions, social organizations and businesses to leverage joint knowledge and resources.
Recruit committed, influential partners from the earliest stages — the same form-cross-sector-partnerships lever with a timing emphasis, not a different intervention.
Build collaborations between academia, industry and social organizations to drive research projects — same intervention.
Core: systemic thinking plus collaborations among actors with commitment, mutual support and enthusiasm.

Pairing visionaries/ideologues with executors is a specific, different matching intervention — the systemic-thinking member and the vision-execution-pairing member share the collaboration topic but not the same lever.
